For people who design and deliver programs

Make the next step
easier to complete.

Four places to investigate in your own program. Each connects a barrier to an action and a measure.

01

Referrals

Already receiving help doesn’t automatically connect a child to WIC.

Try this

Offer a direct referral from Medicaid/SNAP enrollment, with a clear next step and consent-based follow-up.

Evidence and what to measure

Evidence: Descriptive survey evidence; not proof that referrals alone close the gap.

Track: Referral → first appointment → completed enrollment.

Source ↗

02

Enrollment

Families must arrange appointments and provide eligibility information.

Try this

Explain accepted documents before the appointment and identify which information another program can establish.

Evidence and what to measure

Evidence: Documented process and barrier research; evaluate the local change.

Track: Incomplete appointments, repeat document requests, time to enrollment.

Source ↗

03

Shopping

Approval, product rules and store access affect whether food benefits can be used.

Try this

Use product scanning, clear shelf labels and vendor-access reviews to reduce failed purchases.

Evidence and what to measure

Evidence: Retailer-access evidence; electronic benefits have a separate participation study.

Track: Failed purchases, authorized-store access, benefit use by category.

Source ↗

04

Renewal

Support requires continued contact and recertification.

Try this

Give clear renewal reminders, explain what must be updated and check for avoidable repeat tasks.

Evidence and what to measure

Evidence: Documented requirements; do not treat age-group coverage as a renewal rate.

Track: Renewal among still-eligible families, reasons for interruption.

Source ↗

These are actions to evaluate, not a validated score or promises of a particular effect. Avoid collecting personal data you don’t need.
